title: Banana Bread Baked Oatmeal
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Mash bananas (need 1½ cups).
Whisk bananas with brown sugar, eggs, salt, vanilla, baking powder, cinnamon and nutmeg.
Whisk in the milk.
Stir in oats and walnuts.
Pour into a 9×9-inch dish and bake 45 minutes until golden on top and edges.
Serve warm or cold; keeps 5 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen.

seasoning.base: cinnamon, nutmeg, vanilla and a pinch of salt
tryThis: a little extra cinnamon on top before baking
seasoning.tip: The pinch of salt is what makes the banana taste sweeter; don't skip it.

title: Overnight Oats (Base Recipe + Banana Walnut Variation)
steps: Combine oats, brown sugar, cinnamon, chia and salt in an 8 oz jar.
Pour in milk and stir/shake well so nothing clumps.
Lid on, refrigerate 15 minutes to 12 hours (overnight is best).
Top with diced banana and walnuts just before eating. Keeps 4-5 days.
notes: 5 minutes hands-on; total includes ~8 hours chilling.

seasoning.base: cinnamon, a little brown sugar and a pinch of salt
tryThis: a spoon of peanut butter stirred in
seasoning.tip: Mix the cinnamon and salt into the dry oats before adding milk so it doesn't clump.

title: Black Beans with Eggs
steps: Sauté minced garlic and diced jalapeño in olive oil over medium about 1 minute.
Add undrained beans, water and cumin; bring to a simmer.
Simmer about 5 minutes, stirring; smash some beans to thicken.
Lower heat to medium-low, crack eggs onto the beans, partially cover and cook 7-10 minutes, until the whites are set (cook until the yolks are firm for fully cooked eggs).
Top as desired and serve over rice.

seasoning.base: garlic, cumin, salt and black pepper
tryThis: hot sauce or a pinch of chili powder
seasoning.tip: Bloom the cumin and garlic in the oil for 30 seconds before the beans go in.

title: Skillet Breakfast Potatoes
steps: Peel and dice potatoes; cover with water plus 1 tsp salt, bring to a boil and par-boil 5 minutes. Drain.
Dice the onion.
Heat 1 Tbsp oil and the butter in a large skillet over medium; add potatoes in one layer, season with ¼ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper.
Cook undisturbed 4-5 minutes to crisp.
Stir, add remaining oil, onion, garlic powder, onion powder, remaining salt and pepper; cook 7-8 minutes more.
Serve warm (great with eggs).

seasoning.base: salt, black pepper, garlic powder and onion powder
tryThis: Nature's Seasoning instead of plain salt
seasoning.tip: Season after the potatoes start to brown so the spices don't burn.

title: Mexican Red Lentil Stew

ingredients.item: fire roasted diced tomatoes (14.5 oz cans)

steps: Rinse lentils until water runs mostly clear; add 4 cups water, bring to a boil, turn off heat and let sit covered 20 minutes.
Meanwhile sauté diced onion and garlic in olive oil until soft; add diced celery and cook a few minutes.
Add tomatoes with juice, chili powder, cumin, turmeric and hot sauce.
Drain lentils, add to pot with broth; simmer about 15 minutes until thick.
Stir in chopped cilantro and lime juice; adjust salt/hot sauce.

seasoning.base: chili powder, cumin, turmeric and garlic, finished with lime
tryThis: a little chipotle powder for heat
seasoning.tip: Toast the spices in the oil with the onions before adding liquid.

title: Southwest Lentils and Rice Skillet

ingredients.item: black beans, drained & rinsed (15 oz can)

steps: Sauté diced onion in oil 2-3 minutes; add garlic 30 seconds.
Add spices, salt and pepper; toast 30 seconds.
Add lentils, beans, tomatoes with juice, corn and broth; cover, boil, then simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in rice, cover, return to boil, then simmer 20 minutes.
Rest off heat 5 minutes covered, fluff, top with cheese and green onions.

seasoning.base: cumin, chili powder, garlic and salt
seasoning.tip: Bloom the cumin and chili powder in the oil first for deeper flavor.

title: Poor Man's Burrito Bowls
steps: Bring rice, salt and 3 cups water to a boil covered; simmer on low 15 minutes, rest 5 minutes, fluff.
Heat undrained beans with cumin and garlic powder until hot.
Slice green onions and jalapeño.
Build bowls: 1 cup rice, ½ cup beans, ⅓ cup salsa, 1 oz cheese, plus toppings.

seasoning.base: cumin, chili powder, garlic powder and salt
tryThis: lime juice and cilantro on the rice
seasoning.tip: Taste the beans after heating and add salt last; canned beans vary a lot.

title: Vegetable Fried Rice
steps: Prep all vegetables first (keep green-onion whites and greens separate).
Scramble whisked eggs in 2 Tbsp oil over medium; set aside.
On medium-high, stir-fry carrot 2 minutes, add bell pepper and onion whites 1 minute, then peas until hot; set aside.
Add remaining oil, garlic, ginger and cold rice; stir-fry about 2 minutes.
Stir in soy sauce and sesame oil; turn off heat.
Fold in eggs and veggies; top with green onion greens. Any 2 cups frozen mixed veg can sub.

seasoning.base: soy sauce, garlic and ginger
tryThis: a few drops of sesame oil at the end
a pinch of red pepper flakes
seasoning.tip: Use cold day-old rice and add the soy sauce at the end so the rice fries instead of steams.

title: One Pot Chicken and Rice
steps: Mix spices and coat chicken thighs.
Brown thighs in 1 Tbsp oil over medium a few minutes per side (not cooked through); remove.
Lower heat, add remaining oil and onion; sauté 5 minutes, scraping up browned bits.
Add rice and toast 1-2 minutes.
Add broth, set chicken on top, cover and bring to a boil.
Simmer on low 20 minutes without lifting the lid, rest 5 minutes, check the chicken is 165°F, then fluff and serve. Optional: add ½ cup frozen peas with the broth.

seasoning.base: paprika, oregano, thyme, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper
tryThis: Nature's Seasoning on the chicken (skip the ¼ tsp salt if you do)
a squeeze of lemon at the end
seasoning.tip: Season the thighs on both sides and let them sit 15 minutes before browning.

title: Sheet Pan Honey Mustard Chicken and Veggies
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F; cut vegetables.
Stir mayo, mustards, honey, vinegar, garlic powder, paprika, ¼ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper into a sauce.
Toss chicken in the sauce.
Toss potatoes, onion, green beans and carrots with oil and remaining salt/pepper on a sheet pan; spread flat.
Lay chicken on top and pour remaining sauce over it.
Roast 25-30 minutes until chicken reaches 165°F.

seasoning.base: honey, Dijon mustard, garlic, salt and pepper
tryThis: dried thyme or rosemary on the potatoes
seasoning.tip: Salt the potatoes separately so they're seasoned all the way through.

title: Tuna Patties

ingredients.item: chunk light tuna in water, drained (12 oz can)

steps: Chop parsley and green onions; drain tuna well.
Mix tuna, onions, parsley, breadcrumbs, egg, mayo, seasoning salt and lemon juice just until combined.
Shape into 4 patties.
Fry in oil over medium about 5 minutes per side until golden.
Serve over greens or in a pita.

seasoning.base: seasoning salt and lemon juice
tryThis: Old Bay or Nature's Seasoning in place of the seasoning salt (not on top of it)
a little Dijon in the mix
seasoning.tip: Chill the patties 10 minutes before frying so they hold together.

title: Cabbage Soup
steps: Mince garlic; dice onion; slice carrots and celery; dice bell pepper; chop cabbage into 1-inch pieces.
Sauté garlic, onion, carrots, celery and pepper in olive oil over medium until onion softens.
Add tomatoes with juice, tomato sauce, frozen green beans, parsley and spices; cook 1-2 minutes.
Add cabbage and broth; cover, boil, then simmer on medium-low about 40 minutes until cabbage is tender.
Season with salt (start ½ tsp) and stir in lemon juice.

seasoning.base: garlic, smoked paprika, oregano, thyme, salt and pepper
tryThis: a splash of vinegar at the end
seasoning.tip: Add a pinch more salt at the end; cabbage soaks up seasoning.

title: Sheet Pan Chicken Fajitas
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F; mix chili powder, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, cumin, cayenne, sugar and salt.
Cut onions and peppers into ¼-inch strips and slice chicken into thin strips; spread on a large sheet pan.
Drizzle with oil, sprinkle with the seasoning and toss until coated; spread out evenly (don't crowd the pan).
Bake 35-40 minutes, stirring once halfway, until the chicken reaches 165°F (several reviewers find ~30 minutes keeps it juicier; check the temp if you go shorter).
Squeeze half the lime over the top and serve in tortillas with cilantro, sour cream and extra lime.

seasoning.base: fajita seasoning: chili powder, cumin, garlic, paprika and salt
tryThis: a squeeze of lime right out of the oven
seasoning.tip: Toss the chicken and veggies in oil first so the spices stick.

title: Steak Fajitas
notes: Total includes a 30-minute minimum marinade (can marinate up to 1 day in the fridge). Gluten-free with corn tortillas.

ingredients.item: medium limes, zest and juice (about 1½ tsp zest and ¼ cup juice)
red bell peppers, cut into ¼-inch strips
green bell pepper, cut into ¼-inch strips
large yellow onion, cut into ¼-inch strips
flour or corn tortillas, for serving
cilantro, avocado, Greek yogurt or sour cream, queso fresco or feta (optional toppings)

steps: Mix 2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp chili powder, chipotle powder, coriander and 1 tsp salt with the lime zest.
Score the steak in a shallow crosshatch on both sides, rub with the spice mix and put in a zip-top bag.
Whisk lime juice, 2 Tbsp oil, Worcestershire and honey; add to the bag and marinate at least 30 minutes (up to 1 day refrigerated).

Pat steak dry and sear in 1 Tbsp oil in a hot cast-iron skillet 4-6 minutes per side until it reads 145°F (the source pulls it at 140°F and lets the rest carry it up); rest 10 minutes, then slice thinly across the grain.
Sauté peppers and onion in the last 1 Tbsp oil about 8 minutes, add remaining cumin, chili powder and salt and cook 6-8 minutes more; stir in garlic 30 seconds.
Serve steak and veggies in warm tortillas with toppings.

seasoning.base: cumin, chili powder, garlic and lime
seasoning.tip: Marinate at least 30 minutes, then pat dry so the meat sears instead of steams.

title: Sweet and Spicy Glazed Chicken Thighs
steps: Mix brown sugar, cayenne, garlic powder, paprika, salt and pepper.
Pat chicken dry and coat both sides liberally with the mixture.
Heat a large skillet over medium, add oil, and cook chicken 5-7 minutes per side until deeply glazed and 165°F inside.
Cut cayenne to ¼ tsp for less heat; serve with green beans, broccoli or a salad.

seasoning.base: brown sugar, cayenne, paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper
tryThis: a little smoked paprika in the glaze
a squeeze of lime at the end
seasoning.tip: Keep the pan at medium; the brown sugar rub burns on high heat.

title: Chicken Stew

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces (about 6)

steps: Prep onion, celery, garlic, carrots and potatoes; cut chicken into 1-inch pieces and toss with 2 Tbsp flour.
Heat butter and oil in a large pot over medium until sizzling; brown chicken about 5 minutes per side (not cooked through) and remove.
Sauté onion, celery, garlic and carrots about 5 minutes, scraping up the browned bits.
Add remaining 2 Tbsp flour and cook 2 minutes.
Return chicken; add potatoes, herbs, salt, pepper and both broths, stirring to dissolve the flour.
Cover and bring to a boil, then uncover and simmer on medium-low about 30 minutes until potatoes are tender, the gravy thickens and the chicken is 165°F. Season and top with parsley.

seasoning.base: garlic, thyme, rosemary, sage, salt and pepper
tryThis: a bay leaf in the simmer
seasoning.tip: Taste and adjust salt after it simmers; potatoes soak it up.

title: Rib-eye with Steak Pan Potatoes & Peas
notes: Two rib-eye steaks (about 227 g / 8 oz each) are sliced to serve 4.

ingredients.item: rib-eye steaks, about 227 g (8 oz) each and 2 cm thick
olive oil, plus extra for drizzling
radishes, sliced (leaves picked and washed, if any)

steps: Flatten steaks slightly; rub with garlic mixed with the vinegar and a large pinch of salt.
Boil potatoes 8-10 minutes until just tender; drain.
Heat oil and butter in a large non-stick pan over high heat and sear steaks 5-6 minutes per side to at least 145°F; rest on a board at least 3 minutes.
Pan-fry the potatoes in the steak pan until starting to brown.
Blanch peas in boiling water, drain, and add to the pan with radishes for 2 minutes; toss in radish leaves 30 seconds.
Slice steaks thickly, drizzle with a little oil and seasoning to mix with the juices, and serve with the potatoes.

seasoning.base: salt, black pepper and garlic
tryThis: a sprig of rosemary or thyme in the pan
garlic butter to finish the steak
seasoning.tip: Salt the ribeye at least 40 minutes ahead (or right before cooking), never in between.

title: Beefsteak Donburi (Japanese Rice Bowl) with Spinach
notes: About 12 oz of thin-cut ribeye serves 4 over rice.

ingredients.item: medium garlic cloves (8 halved, 1 minced), divided
bunch spinach, washed and spun dry (10 oz)
ribeye steaks, about ½ inch thick (about 12 oz total)
scallions, thinly sliced on a bias
kizami nori and beni shoga (pickled ginger), optional

steps: Fry the halved garlic in oil in a 10-inch cast-iron skillet over medium until golden, about 7 minutes; reserve.
Wilt spinach with salt about 5 minutes; off heat add minced garlic, sesame oil and vinegar. Set aside and wipe the skillet.

Heat skillet until just smoking; season steaks (optionally rub one side with mayo) and sear 2 minutes, flip and cook 1 minute more (source cooks these thin steaks rare-medium-rare; for 145°F give them another minute or two); rest at least 3 minutes.
Deglaze with sake 1 minute; add dashi, soy sauce, mirin and fried garlic; simmer 4 minutes, thicken with slurry, then swirl in butter off heat.
Divide rice into bowls, top with sliced steak, sauce, spinach and garlic; garnish with scallions (and nori/ginger if using).

seasoning.base: soy sauce, garlic and a little sugar
tryThis: a pinch of red pepper flakes
seasoning.tip: Have the pan very hot and sear in batches so the thin beef browns.

title: Bacon & Egg Breakfast Tacos
notes: Source time assumes the bacon is already cooked crispy; allow extra time to cook it.

ingredients.item: bacon, cooked crispy and coarsely chopped

steps: Cook bacon until crispy and chop; warm the tortillas.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high; scramble eggs with salt until cooked through.
Sprinkle cheese over the eggs and remove from heat.
Fill tortillas with eggs, bacon, tomatoes and avocado; top with cilantro.
Make-ahead: cooked egg-bacon filling keeps 3 days in the fridge.

seasoning.base: salt, black pepper and a little garlic powder
seasoning.tip: Season the eggs while they cook; the bacon adds salt, so go light.

title: Southwest Breakfast Skillet

ingredients.item: Yukon Gold or red potatoes, cut into ½-inch pieces
medium red, orange or yellow bell pepper, diced
Swiss chard, stemmed and thinly sliced (1 bunch)

steps: Cook bacon in a large nonstick skillet over medium 5-7 minutes until crisp; drain and pour off all but 2 tsp fat.
Cook potatoes 2 minutes, add water, cover and steam 5 minutes.
Add mushrooms, bell pepper, onion and ⅛ tsp each salt and pepper; cook about 5 minutes until tender.
Stir in chard and garlic about 2 minutes until wilted; crumble in the bacon.
Make 4 wells, crack an egg into each, season, cover and cook about 5 minutes until whites are set (a few minutes more for firm yolks).
Top with cheese, cilantro and salsa.

seasoning.base: salt, black pepper and garlic
tryThis: cumin or chili powder on the potatoes
seasoning.tip: Bacon is salty; taste before adding more salt.

title: J D's Ham Tacos
steps: Heat the ham until hot.
Lightly fry corn tortillas in corn oil.
While the tortillas and ham are still hot, add them together with the sharp cheese so the cheese melts.
Top with tomato slices and lettuce.
Salt the tomatoes when you plate.

seasoning.base: light salt on the tomatoes; the ham and sharp cheese carry the rest

title: J D's Microwave Baked Potatoes
steps: Poke holes all over the potatoes with a fork.
Microwave on high: 8 minutes for 1 potato, plus 1 minute for each extra potato (2 potatoes = 9 minutes, 3 = 10 minutes).
Remove the potatoes from the microwave. Careful, they're hot!
Put the potatoes on a plate and mash them flat with a fork, mixing in butter and cream cheese.
Season with garlic and a light sprinkle of salt.
Top with shredded sharp cheddar, then sprinkle Nature's Seasoning on top of the cheese.
Microwave until the cheese melts.
Cut a bite with your fork and eat. Enjoy!

seasoning.base: garlic, light salt and Nature's Seasoning
tryThis: a sprinkle of chives or green onion

title: Grilled Skirt Steak Fajitas
notes: Source yield is 4 to 6 servings. Total time includes at least 3 hours marinating (up to 10 hours). Written for a charcoal grill.

ingredients.item: medium cloves garlic, finely minced (about 1 Tbsp)
trimmed skirt steak (about 1 whole steak), cut crosswise into 5- to 6-inch pieces
large red bell pepper, cut into ½-inch strips
large yellow bell pepper, cut into ½-inch strips
large green bell pepper, cut into ½-inch strips
white or yellow onion, cut into ½-inch slices
fresh flour or corn tortillas, hot
sour cream, shredded cheese and salsa, for serving (optional)

steps: Whisk soy sauce, lime juice, oil, brown sugar, chili powder, garlic, cumin and pepper. Set ½ cup of this marinade aside.
Put steak and the rest of the marinade in a zip-top bag; refrigerate 3 to 10 hours, turning now and then.
Toss peppers and onion with the reserved ½ cup marinade and refrigerate.
Wipe excess marinade off the steak. Build a hot charcoal fire on one side of the grill; clean and oil the grate.

Grill steak over the hot side, flipping every minute with the lid on, until charred and 145°F inside (the source pulls it at 115-120°F medium-rare or 125-130°F medium, below the 145°F safety standard). Rest 10-15 minutes.
Cook peppers and onion in a cast-iron skillet on the hot side about 10 minutes until charred in spots; pour in the steak juices.
Slice steak thin against the grain and serve with the veggies, hot tortillas and toppings.

seasoning.base: soy sauce, lime, chili powder, cumin, garlic and black pepper
seasoning.tip: Wipe off excess marinade before grilling so the steak chars instead of steams.

title: The Food Lab's Perfect Grilled Steaks (Ribeye)
notes: Source says 3 to 4 servings (2 large steaks). Total includes the 40-minute salt rest; steaks can rest salted in the fridge up to 4 days. Written for a charcoal grill. Bone-in steaks about 1 lb each, or boneless about 12 oz.

ingredients.item: large ribeye or strip steaks, 1½ to 2 inches thick (about 2 lb total)
kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

steps: Salt the steaks well and let them rest at least 40 minutes (or up to 4 days uncovered on a rack in the fridge).
Build a charcoal fire on one side of the grill; clean and oil the grate.
Pepper the steaks and cook on the cool side, lid on, flipping every few minutes, until about 125°F, 10-15 minutes (source: 105°F for medium-rare, 115°F for medium).
Move to the hot side and sear, flipping often, about 2 minutes until charred and 145°F inside (source stops at 125°F medium-rare or 135°F medium).
Rest 5-10 minutes (at least 3), then slice and serve.

seasoning.base: salt, black pepper and garlic
tryThis: a little garlic powder in the rub
a pat of garlic butter to finish
seasoning.tip: Salt at least 40 minutes ahead (up to overnight uncovered in the fridge).

title: Grilled Chicken Thighs with Chicken Thigh Marinade
notes: Total includes a 30-minute marinade; you can marinate up to 12 hours in the fridge (4-6 hours is ideal). The page also gives oven directions (425°F, 15-25 minutes).

ingredients.item: small limes, juice and zest (about 3 Tbsp juice and 1 tsp zest)

steps: Mix garlic, oil, honey, soy sauce, Worcestershire, Dijon, cumin, salt, cayenne, lime juice and zest in a bowl or zip-top bag.
Add chicken and coat. Marinate 30 minutes at room temp or up to 12 hours in the fridge. Let stand 15 minutes before cooking.
Heat grill to medium-high (about 400°F), scrub and oil the grates.
Grill smooth-side down 8-12 minutes, flipping once, until 165°F at the thickest part.
Cover and rest 5-10 minutes, then eat.

seasoning.base: garlic, lime, cumin, soy sauce and a pinch of cayenne
tryThis: fajita seasoning instead of the spices
seasoning.tip: Marinate at least 30 minutes; pat dry before grilling for better char.

title: Grilled Chicken Fajitas (Foil Packets)
notes: Makes 6 foil packets. Cleanup is just the foil.

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into ½-inch strips
red (or yellow or orange) bell peppers, cut into ½-inch strips
red onion, cut into ½-inch slices
flour or whole wheat tortillas, for serving

steps: Heat grill to medium/medium-high (about 450°F).
Toss chicken, peppers, onion and zucchini in a big bowl with lime juice and all the spices.
Spray 6 large sheets of heavy-duty foil, divide the mix among them, and fold into tightly sealed packets (leave room inside for steam).
Grill 8-12 minutes until the chicken is 165°F (no pink left) and veggies are crisp-tender.
Open carefully (hot steam) and serve with warm tortillas and toppings.

seasoning.base: fajita seasoning: chili powder, cumin, garlic and salt
tryThis: a squeeze of lime when you open the packets
seasoning.tip: Toss everything with the lime juice and spices in the bowl, and spray the foil well so nothing sticks.

title: Pressure Cooker (Instant Pot) Hard Boiled Eggs
notes: Makes 12 eggs. Needs a steamer basket or trivet.
steps: Put a steamer basket in the pot, add the water, and set the eggs in the basket.
Lock the lid; cook on High Pressure 6 minutes.
Let pressure release naturally 6 minutes, then quick-release the rest.
Move the eggs to ice-cold water for 6 minutes to stop the cooking.

seasoning.base: salt and black pepper
seasoning.tip: Season right after peeling while the eggs are still a little warm.

title: Instant Pot Egg Bites (Ham or Bacon)
notes: Makes 14 egg bites. Needs two silicone baby-food/egg-bite trays, a trivet and a sling.

ingredients.item: diced ham or precooked bacon (or both!)

steps: Spray two silicone trays well. Whisk eggs, milk, salt and pepper.
Divide the ham/bacon among the cups, pour egg over until each is about ⅔ full, and top with cheddar.
Pour 1 cup water into the pot, add the trivet, and lower the stacked trays in with a sling.
Cook on High Pressure 11 minutes (a minute or two less for softer eggs).
Natural release 5 minutes, then quick release. Cool on a rack 5 minutes and pop the bites out.

seasoning.base: salt, black pepper and garlic powder
seasoning.tip: Ham and bacon are salty; go light on added salt.

title: Instant Pot 15 Bean Soup (with Ham)
notes: Source yield is 8 to 10 servings. Total includes a 1-hour quick soak inside the pot. No-soak option on the page: 35 minutes High Pressure with a 10-minute natural release.

ingredients.item: package Hurst's HamBeens 15 Bean Soup with seasoning packet (20 oz)
can crushed tomatoes in puree (15 oz)
salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

steps: Set the seasoning packet aside; rinse and pick over the beans.
Sauté oil, onion and celery about 3 minutes; add garlic for 1 minute.
Add beans, 2 quarts water and the ham bone. High Pressure 1 minute, then let the beans soak 1 hour without releasing pressure.
Stir in tomatoes, carrots, chili powder and the seasoning packet. High Pressure 3 minutes.
Natural release 10 minutes, then quick release.
Remove the ham bone; stir in spinach, diced ham and lemon juice and let it heat through (ham to 140°F). Salt and pepper to taste.

seasoning.base: the ham seasoning packet, garlic, onion, chili powder, salt and pepper
tryThis: a little Cajun seasoning (go light; the packet and ham are already salty)
seasoning.tip: Add salt at the end; the ham adds plenty while it cooks.

title: Instant Pot Black Beans
notes: Makes about 6 cups. No soaking needed.

ingredients.item: dried black beans (about 2 cups, no need to soak)
green bell pepper, cored, seeded and diced
optional for serving: diced avocado, jalapeño, red onion, cilantro, cherry tomatoes

steps: Rinse the beans and pick out any stones or bad beans.
Sauté oil, onion, bell pepper and salt 4-6 minutes until soft. Stir in cumin, oregano, bay leaves and garlic for 30 seconds.
Add water and beans. Seal and cook on High Pressure 35 minutes.
Let pressure release naturally 20 minutes. Remove bay leaves. Eat warm or portion and store.

seasoning.base: garlic, cumin, oregano, onion and salt
seasoning.tip: The recipe salts the veggies up front; taste the cooked beans and add more salt only if needed.

title: Instant Pot Peanut-Lime Chicken Thighs
notes: Source yield is 4 to 6 servings. Written for a 6-quart pot; in an 8-quart or larger pot add about ½ cup more broth.

ingredients.item: freeze-dried cilantro OR 3 Tbsp fresh diced cilantro

steps: On Sauté, brown the chicken in oil in small batches; set aside.
Add broth, soy sauce, cilantro, lime juice, pepper flakes and ginger; scrape the bottom. Stir in peanut butter.
Return chicken and juices. High Pressure 9 minutes, then quick release.
Take out the chicken (it should read 165°F). Stir cornstarch + 2 Tbsp water into the sauce and simmer until thick; put the chicken back and coat.
Serve over rice with peanuts, green onions and lime.

seasoning.base: garlic, ginger, soy sauce and lime
seasoning.tip: Brown the thighs on Saute first for more flavor.

title: Healthy Banana Muffins
notes: Makes 12 muffins. One bowl.

ingredients.item: canola oil (or melted and cooled coconut oil)
walnut halves, toasted and coarsely chopped

steps: Heat oven to 350°F with a rack in the upper third. Line or grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Mash bananas in a big bowl. Whisk in egg, yogurt and oil, then brown sugar, maple syrup and vanilla.
Sprinkle on baking soda, salt and cinnamon and stir.
Gently stir in flour until barely combined; fold in walnuts.
Fill cups nearly to the top and bake 20-22 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.

seasoning.base: cinnamon, vanilla and a pinch of salt
tryThis: a sprinkle of cinnamon sugar on top

title: Ham and Cheese Quiche
notes: Uses 1 pie crust (homemade or store-bought) in a standard 9-inch pie dish.

ingredients.item: shredded cheese such as Gruyère or white cheddar (about ¾ cup)

steps: Heat oven to 375°F. Roll crust into an 11-inch circle and fit it into a 9-inch pie dish; crimp the edge.
Line with foil, fill with pie weights or dried beans, bake 10 minutes; remove foil and bake 3 minutes more. Lower oven to 350°F.
Whisk eggs, milk, mustard, salt, pepper, nutmeg and hot sauce.
Scatter ham, cheese and green onion in the crust and pour the egg mix over.
Bake on a rimmed sheet 40-50 minutes until the center is set (cover the crust edge with foil if it browns too fast). Rest 5-10 minutes and slice.

seasoning.base: salt, black pepper and a pinch of nutmeg
seasoning.tip: Ham and cheese are salty; use less added salt.

title: Healthy Oatmeal Cookies
notes: Makes 24 cookies. Source lists 20 minutes total, but the dough also needs at least 30 minutes in the fridge (up to 3 days).

ingredients.item: well chopped raw walnuts or pecans

steps: Whisk oats, flour, baking powder, cinnamon and salt in a big bowl.
In another bowl whisk applesauce, butter, egg, vanilla and honey.
Stir wet into dry just until combined (dough is sticky). Fold in chocolate chips, raisins and nuts.
Chill at least 30 minutes (up to 3 days).
Heat oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet. Drop 1½-inch balls 1 inch apart and flatten to ¾ inch thick.
Bake 9-10 minutes until golden at the edges. Cool 2 minutes on the pan, then on a rack.

seasoning.base: cinnamon, vanilla and a pinch of salt
tryThis: a flake of sea salt on top

title: Baked Chicken Thighs
notes: Total includes a 30-minute marinade (or up to 12 hours in the fridge). One sheet pan.

ingredients.item: yellow onion, halved and thinly sliced lengthwise
chopped fresh parsley, tarragon or thyme, plus more for serving

steps: Pat chicken dry. Mix garlic, 2 Tbsp oil, paprika, Italian seasoning, lemon zest and juice, 1 tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper; coat the chicken. Marinate 30 minutes (or up to 12 hours in the fridge).
Heat oven to 425°F. Put onions on a parchment-lined sheet pan with the last 1 Tbsp oil, ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper; spread out.
Nestle the chicken (excess marinade shaken off) among the onions.
Bake 15 minutes, stir the onions, then bake 10-20 minutes more until the chicken is 165°F. Rest 5 minutes.
Broil 1-2 minutes to crisp the skin (watch it). Top with herbs and serve with the onions and pan juices.

seasoning.base: salt, black pepper, garlic and paprika
seasoning.tip: Season the thighs 30 minutes ahead and pat dry for crispier skin.

title: Scrambled Eggs with Rice
notes: One skillet. Uses already-cooked rice (day-old rice, warmed a little, works best). Source suggests adding sliced ham if you like.

ingredients.item: gochujang (or to taste; chile oil or sriracha also work)

steps: Beat the eggs with a fork.
Heat oil in a big non-stick skillet over medium-low. Scramble the eggs lightly, leaving them a bit runny; stir in the gochujang.
Stir in the warm rice, breaking up clumps, and cook a few minutes until hot and the eggs are fully set.
Stir in soy sauce and sesame oil. Top with green onions and eat.

seasoning.base: salt, black pepper and soy sauce
seasoning.tip: Season the eggs gently and take them off the heat while still a little soft.

title: Dollar Store Dinners: Bean Quesadillas and Spanish Rice
notes: Serving = 2 quesadillas + 1 cup rice. Seven ingredients, about $2.19 a serving per the source. Taco seasoning can replace the Bayou Blend (add salt if it has none).

ingredients.item: can Rotel (diced tomatoes with chiles) (10 oz)

steps: Thaw and drain the frozen veggies; rinse and drain the beans; shred the cheese.
Mix veggies, beans, cheese and seasoning in a bowl. Taste and adjust.
Drain the Rotel juice into a measuring cup and add water to make 2 cups (or what the rice packet says).
Put rice, drained tomatoes and liquid in a pot, cover, boil, then simmer on medium-low about 7 minutes. Turn off.
Spread a scant ½ cup filling on half of each tortilla and fold.
Cook in a dry skillet over medium until crispy and melty. Cut and serve with the rice.

seasoning.base: Bayou Blend (or taco) seasoning, plus the seasoned rice packet
seasoning.tip: Taste the filling before adding salt; the seasoning blend and packet rice are already salty.

title: Breakfast Quesadilla
notes: Makes 8 quesadillas. Freezer-friendly: wrap each one, freeze up to 2 months, and microwave 2-3 minutes from frozen.

ingredients.item: lightly packed fresh spinach, roughly torn (about 4 oz)
whole wheat tortillas (medium taco size, about 7 inches)

steps: Whisk eggs, milk, salt, garlic powder and pepper.
Heat oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium; wilt the spinach about 1 minute. Add beans, turn to medium-low, pour in eggs and scramble slowly about 5 minutes until just set.
Sprinkle each tortilla with ⅛ of the cheese, add ⅛ of the eggs, and fold in half.
Wipe the skillet, spray it, and cook quesadillas over medium 5-6 minutes total until golden and melted. Cut and serve.
To freeze: cool filling first, wrap each quesadilla, freeze flat, then bag.

seasoning.base: salt, black pepper and garlic powder

title: Egg Roll in a Bowl
notes: One pan, about 6½ cups. Bagged broccoli slaw means almost no chopping.

ingredients.item: canola, grapeseed or other neutral high-heat oil
fresh ginger, minced (or 1 tsp ground ginger)
chili paste (sambal oelek) or hot sauce of choice, plus more to taste
to serve (optional): prepared brown rice, quinoa or cauliflower rice

steps: Whisk 1 Tbsp soy sauce with the cornstarch, stir in the turkey, and let sit 10 minutes.
Finely chop mushrooms, mince garlic, slice green onions.
Heat oil in a wok or big deep pan over high; cook turkey, breaking it up, about 5 minutes until no pink remains and it reaches 165°F.
Add most of the green onions and the mushrooms; cook 2 minutes.
Turn to medium-low; add slaw, carrots, ginger and garlic and stir-fry 2 minutes.
Add vinegar, chili paste, sesame oil, pepper and the last 2 Tbsp soy sauce; cook 1 minute. Serve as-is or over rice, topped with green onions.

seasoning.base: garlic, ginger and soy sauce
seasoning.tip: Add the soy sauce at the end so the cabbage doesn't go soggy.

title: Biscuits and Gravy Bake
notes: One skillet; the biscuit dough has sharp cheddar mixed in.
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Brown the sausage in an oven-safe skillet over medium heat until cooked through (160°F).
Stir in 2 Tbsp butter, then ¼ cup flour; cook 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in 3 cups milk, salt and pepper; stir 3-5 minutes until thick. Take off heat.
Whisk 2 cups flour, baking powder, sugar, salt and parsley; cut in the cold butter until crumbly.
Stir in milk and cheddar just until a thick, spoonable dough forms.
Drop about 10 spoonfuls of dough over the hot gravy, brush with melted butter, and bake 25-28 minutes until golden and cooked through. Rest 5 minutes.

seasoning.base: black pepper, salt and a pinch of sage
tryThis: red pepper flakes in the gravy
seasoning.tip: Be generous with black pepper in the gravy; that's its signature.

title: Scalloped Potatoes
notes: Makes about 9 one-cup servings; good side for ham or steak.

ingredients.item: salt, divided (6 tsp for boiling water)

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a 9×9 dish. Peel and slice potatoes ¼ inch thick; boil 5 minutes in a gallon of water with 6 tsp salt, then drain.
Warm milk and broth together until barely steaming.
Melt butter in a saucepan, stir in flour and cook until bubbly; whisk in the hot milk mixture and bring to a boil.
Season with remaining ½ tsp salt, pepper, onion and garlic powder, nutmeg and cayenne; cook 2 minutes more.
Layer half the potatoes and half the sauce, then repeat, spreading sauce to the edges.
Bake covered with foil 30 minutes, then uncovered 30 minutes until golden and tender. Cool 15 minutes.

seasoning.base: salt, black pepper, garlic and a pinch of nutmeg
tryThis: a little dry mustard in the sauce
seasoning.tip: The potatoes are boiled in well-salted water and the butter is salted, so taste the sauce before adding more salt.

title: Hasselback Potatoes
notes: One potato each. Top with butter, sharp cheddar, or Nature's Seasoning if you like.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with parchment. Wash and dry the potatoes.
Lay each potato flat with a chopstick on each side and cut thin slices (⅛-¼ inch) without cutting all the way through.
Whisk oil, salt, pepper and garlic powder; brush about half over the potatoes.
Bake 35 minutes, baste with the rest of the oil between the layers, then bake 35 minutes more.
Check that the middle is tender and serve warm with your favorite toppings.

seasoning.base: salt, black pepper and garlic
seasoning.tip: Brush the seasoned oil between the slices halfway through baking.

title: Instant Pot Mashed Potatoes
notes: Serving is 1 cup. Total includes about 30 minutes to come to pressure. Try stirring in cream cheese, garlic and sharp cheddar, J D style.

ingredients.item: russet potatoes, peeled and cut into large cubes

steps: Peel the potatoes and cut into large cubes.
Put them in the Instant Pot, cover with 6 cups water and sprinkle in 2 tsp salt.
Seal the valve and pressure cook 12 minutes (it takes about 30 minutes to come to pressure).
Carefully quick-release the steam, then drain the potatoes in a colander.
Return to the pot with the remaining salt, pepper and butter, slowly add the warm milk, and mash gently (don't over-mash or they get gummy).

seasoning.base: salt, black pepper, butter and garlic
tryThis: cream cheese and sharp cheddar, J D style
seasoning.tip: Salt the cooking water; potatoes absorb it while they cook.

title: Grilled Corn on the Cob
notes: One cob each. Easy side for grilled ribeye, fajitas or chicken thighs.
steps: Soak the corn in cool water at least 10 minutes.
Peel the husks back halfway, pull out only the silks, then fold the husks back over the corn.
Lightly oil the grill and grill on high heat, turning every 2-4 minutes until the husks are charred on all sides.
Serve with melted butter and a sprinkle of salt, using the peeled-back husk as a handle.

seasoning.base: butter and salt

title: Grilled Chicken Thighs
notes: Total includes at least 30 minutes marinating (up to 4 hours). Boneless thighs, so they grill fast.
steps: Mix the oil, brown sugar, balsamic, Dijon, soy sauce, lemon pepper, rosemary and garlic in a bowl or zip-top bag.
Add the thighs and marinate 30 minutes to 4 hours in the fridge.
Grill over medium-high heat about 5-7 minutes a side, until 165°F inside.
Let rest 5 minutes, then serve.

seasoning.base: lemon pepper, rosemary, garlic and Dijon
tryThis: Nature's Seasoning instead of lemon pepper
a pinch of red pepper flakes
seasoning.tip: Don't marinate past 4 hours; the vinegar starts to change the texture.

title: Best Steak Marinade in Existence
notes: Makes about 1⅓ cups of marinade, enough for several steaks; time is just mixing, so add marinating and grilling time. Works on ribeye, or on cheaper cuts like flank or sirloin.
steps: Put everything in a blender and blend about 30 seconds until combined.
Pour over steaks in a bag or dish and marinate in the fridge, then grill to at least 145°F and rest 3 minutes.
Leftover marinade keeps up to 5 days in the fridge (unused, not after raw meat).

seasoning.base: garlic, soy, Worcestershire, lemon and white pepper
tryThis: swap white pepper for cracked black pepper
a shake of Nature's Seasoning on the steak just before grilling
seasoning.tip: Soy sauce is salty, so skip extra salt; pat the steak dry before it hits the grill for a better crust.

title: Easy Chicken Fajita Marinade
notes: Total includes 4 hours marinating (can go overnight). Source uses chicken breast strips; boneless thighs work too and stay juicier. Serve in warm corn tortillas with peppers and onions.

ingredients.item: boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into strips

steps: Whisk the oil, chili powder, lime juice, honey, garlic powder, paprika and pepper.
Put the chicken strips in a zip-top bag, pour in the marinade, squeeze out the air and refrigerate 4 hours to overnight.
Heat the grill to medium-high and oil the grate; lift the chicken out and toss the used marinade.
Grill about 10 minutes per side, turning once, until browned and the thickest strip reads 165°F.

seasoning.base: chili powder, garlic, lime and a little honey
tryThis: fajita seasoning in place of the chili powder
light salt or Nature's Seasoning, since the marinade has none
seasoning.tip: Add a little salt to the marinade or to the meat right off the grill; the recipe has none.

title: Grilled Chicken Marinade
notes: Total includes 2 hours marinating (up to 4). Source uses thin-sliced chicken breasts; boneless chicken thighs work and take a few minutes longer per side.

ingredients.item: skinless boneless chicken breasts, thinly sliced

steps: Whisk the vinegar, soy sauce, oil, herbs, garlic powder and pepper.
Bag the chicken with the marinade and refrigerate 2 to 4 hours.
Heat the grill to medium-low and oil the grate; drain off the marinade.
Grill about 4-5 minutes a side, until 165°F inside.

seasoning.base: garlic, oregano, basil, parsley and black pepper
tryThis: a pinch of red pepper flakes
a squeeze of lemon after grilling
seasoning.tip: Medium-low heat keeps thin chicken from drying out; thighs can take medium.

title: Instant Pot Salsa Chicken
notes: Starts from frozen chicken breasts; boneless thighs work too. Total includes coming to pressure and about 20 minutes natural release. Use it in corn tortillas, burrito bowls, quesadillas or on a baked potato. Check the taco seasoning label if you need it gluten-free; some packets contain wheat.

ingredients.item: frozen skinless boneless chicken breast halves

steps: Put the chicken in the Instant Pot and coat all sides with the taco seasoning.
Pour the salsa and broth over the top.
Seal and cook on the Poultry setting for 15 minutes (it takes 10-15 minutes to come to pressure).
Let the pressure release naturally, about 20 minutes, then open.
Check the chicken reads 165°F (it starts frozen), then shred it in the sauce and serve however you like.

seasoning.base: taco seasoning (chili, cumin, garlic) and salsa
tryThis: fajita seasoning instead of taco seasoning
a squeeze of lime after shredding
a pinch of chipotle powder for smoke
seasoning.tip: Taco packets are salty; taste after shredding before adding any salt.

title: Instant Pot Chicken Tikka Masala with Cauliflower and Peas
notes: Made with boneless chicken thighs; lightened up with coconut milk. Dairy-free only if you use coconut oil instead of the ghee or butter. Serve over rice.

ingredients.item: ghee or butter (coconut oil to keep it dairy-free)

steps: Toss the chicken with 1 tsp of the salt.
On Saute, melt the ghee and cook the onion, garlic, ginger and all six spices 2-3 minutes until soft and fragrant.
Blend in the tomatoes until smooth, stir in the chicken and the rest of the salt, then pressure cook 15 minutes on high (chicken to 165°F).
Quick release, add the cauliflower and peas, and pressure cook 2 more minutes.
Quick release, stir in the coconut milk and top with cilantro.

seasoning.base: garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric and garam masala
tryThis: a squeeze of lime at the end
a pinch of sugar if the tomatoes taste sharp
seasoning.tip: Bloom the spices in the ghee on Saute before adding tomatoes; that's where the flavor comes from.

title: Instant Pot White Chicken Chili
notes: 1-cup servings. Uses cream cheese, one of J D's favorites; boneless chicken thighs can stand in for the breasts. Good over a baked potato. Check the ranch packet label if you need it gluten-free.

ingredients.item: can black beans, drained and rinsed
can Rotel diced tomatoes with green chilies, with juice
packet ranch dip or dressing mix
tortilla chips or baked potatoes, to serve

steps: Layer the chicken, beans, onion, corn, Rotel and broth in the Instant Pot.
Sprinkle in the chili powder, cumin and ranch mix and stir so some liquid gets under the chicken.
Set the cream cheese pieces on top, seal and pressure cook 20 minutes on high; natural release 10 minutes, then vent.
Check the chicken is 165°F, shred it, stir the melted cream cheese through the chili, return the chicken and serve with toppings.

seasoning.base: cumin, chili powder, garlic and onion from the ranch mix
tryThis: a pinch of cayenne or diced jalapeño
seasoning.tip: Ranch mix and Rotel are salty, so taste before adding salt.

title: Twice Baked Potatoes
notes: 12 halves from 6 small russets. Bacon and sharp cheddar, close to J D's baked potato style; make ahead and bake the second time when needed.

ingredients.item: chopped fresh chives or green onions

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Scrub and fork-poke the potatoes and bake 50-60 minutes until tender; cool a bit.
Halve them lengthwise and scoop out the insides, leaving a thin shell.
Mash the potato with sour cream, butter, garlic powder, salt and pepper, adding warm milk only if needed.
Fold in the bacon, chives and half the cheddar.
Fill the skins, top with the rest of the cheese and bake 15-20 minutes until hot and melty.

seasoning.base: garlic powder, salt and black pepper, plus bacon and sharp cheddar
tryThis: swap in cream cheese for some of the sour cream, J D style
Nature's Seasoning on top of the cheese
seasoning.tip: Rub the skins with a little oil and salt before the first bake for crispier shells.

title: Crispy and Tender Baked Chicken Thighs
notes: Bone-in, skin-on thighs with a simple dry rub and no oil needed. A plainer, crispier take than the Well Plated baked thighs with onions.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with sprayed foil.
Lay the thighs skin-side up on the sheet.
Mix the garlic salt, onion salt, oregano, thyme, paprika and pepper and sprinkle it generously over the chicken.
Bake about 1 hour, until the skin is crisp and the thighs reach 165°F near the bone.

seasoning.base: garlic salt, onion salt, oregano, thyme, paprika and black pepper
tryThis: Nature's Seasoning as the whole rub
seasoning.tip: Pat the skin dry and season an hour ahead (or overnight uncovered in the fridge) for crispier skin.

title: Hibachi-Style Fried Rice
notes: Garlic-heavy and done in 20 minutes; great way to use leftover grilled chicken (or chopped ham or fajita meat). Different from the Budget Bytes Vegetable Fried Rice: no veg, lots of garlic and egg.
steps: Heat the oil in a wok or nonstick skillet over medium-high and scramble the eggs 2-3 minutes.
Add the chicken, green onion and garlic and stir about 2 minutes until hot (leftover chicken to 165°F).
Stir in the rice until warm, about 2 minutes.
Add the soy sauce and toss about 3 minutes until evenly coated.

seasoning.base: garlic, soy sauce and green onion
tryThis: a little butter at the end, hibachi style
a few drops of sesame oil
seasoning.tip: Use cold leftover rice so it fries instead of going mushy.

title: Southwest Breakfast Burritos
notes: Makes 20 small burritos to freeze; microwave one 3-4 minutes for a fast breakfast. Swap the sausage for diced ham or bacon if you like.
steps: Whisk the eggs, milk and salt; scramble in the butter until set, then break into small pieces in a big bowl.
In the same skillet cook the sausage with the garlic about 5 minutes, add the onion and cook until crumbly and no pink remains (160°F); drain.
Mix the sausage into the eggs with the tomato, cilantro, jalapeños and taco seasoning; cool, then stir in the cheddar.
Fill and roll each tortilla into a tight burrito.
Wrap each one and freeze; reheat in the microwave 3-4 minutes until hot in the center (165°F).

seasoning.base: taco seasoning, garlic and salt
tryThis: a dash of hot sauce before rolling
Nature's Seasoning on the eggs (go light; the taco packet and sausage are salty)
seasoning.tip: Let the filling cool before adding cheese and rolling so the tortillas don't get soggy.

title: Chicken Fajitas (Skillet)
notes: Makes 8 fajitas in a cast-iron skillet, no grill needed. Source uses chicken breast cutlets; boneless thighs work and cook a little longer. Corn tortillas are fine instead of flour.

ingredients.item: large boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 1½ lb)
bell peppers, sliced ¼ inch thick
lime wedges, cilantro, sour cream, pico de gallo, guacamole and shredded cheddar, for serving

steps: Stir 2 Tbsp oil, the lime juice and all the spices together in a bowl.
Halve the chicken breasts into thin cutlets and coat them in the mix (up to 4 hours ahead).
Sear the chicken in 1 Tbsp oil in a heavy skillet over medium, 3-5 minutes a side to 165°F; rest it on a board.
Cook the peppers and onion in the last 1 Tbsp oil 5-6 minutes until browned in spots; season.
Slice the chicken, toss it back in with the veggies, and serve in warm tortillas with toppings.

seasoning.base: chili powder, cumin, paprika, garlic, onion powder, salt and pepper
tryThis: store-bought fajita seasoning in a pinch
seasoning.tip: Mix the spices with the oil and lime so they coat the chicken evenly and don't scorch.

title: Best Egg Salad
notes: Cheap, high-protein lunch. Use the Instant Pot Hard Boiled Eggs recipe for the eggs. Eat on toast, in a wrap or with crackers.
steps: Hard-boil, chill, peel and chop the eggs (chunky is good).
Add the celery, red onion, dill and chives.
Stir the mayo, lemon, Dijon, garlic, salt, paprika and pepper together in another bowl.
Fold the dressing into the eggs, taste, adjust seasoning and serve.

seasoning.base: garlic, Dijon, paprika, salt and black pepper
tryThis: Nature's Seasoning instead of plain salt
seasoning.tip: The dressing already has salt; taste after mixing and add more only if needed.

title: Easy Microwave Chocolate Mug Cake
notes: One serving, made with pantry staples in a big mug. Microwaves vary; start checking at about 1½ minutes.
steps: Whisk the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda and salt right in a large microwave-safe mug.
Stir in the milk, oil, water and vanilla until smooth.
Microwave about 1 minute 45 seconds, until the middle is set.
Let it cool a minute and eat from the mug.

seasoning.base: cocoa, vanilla and a pinch of salt
tryThis: a spoon of peanut butter dropped in the middle
seasoning.tip: Don't skip the pinch of salt; it makes the chocolate taste richer.

title: Rice Krispie Treats
notes: No-bake. Allow about 1 more hour to cool before cutting. Keeps 3 days covered at room temperature (not the fridge).

ingredients.item: unsalted butter, plus more for the pan

steps: Butter a 9×9 pan and line it with parchment.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium-low, add 6 cups marshmallows and stir just until melted.
Off the heat, stir in vanilla and salt, then the cereal, then fold in the last 2 cups marshmallows.
Press lightly into the pan under a sheet of parchment.
Cool to room temperature, about 1 hour, then cut into squares.

seasoning.base: vanilla and a little sea salt
tryThis: a spoon of peanut butter melted in with the marshmallows
a drizzle of chocolate syrup on top
seasoning.tip: Keep the heat low; overcooked marshmallows make hard treats.

title: Classic Peanut Butter Cookies
notes: Makes 4 dozen. Total includes 1 hour chilling the dough. Freeze extra dough balls and bake a few at a time. Don't eat the raw dough (raw egg and flour).
steps: Beat the butter, peanut butter and both sugars until smooth, then beat in the eggs.
Sift the flour, baking soda, baking powder and salt into it and stir just until combined; chill the dough 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 375°F, roll 1-inch balls, set them 2 inches apart and press a crisscross with a fork.
Bake 7-10 minutes until the edges are golden; cool briefly on the pan, then on a rack.

seasoning.base: a little salt to balance the peanut butter and sugar
tryThis: a sprinkle of flaky salt before baking
a pinch of cinnamon in the dough
a drizzle of honey on warm cookies
seasoning.tip: Chill the dough the full hour so the cookies don't spread flat.

title: J D's Banana Peanut Butter Scoop
steps: Peel the banana and split it lengthwise down the middle, like a banana split, and lay the halves in a bowl or on a plate.
Add a scoop of peanut butter on top.
Drizzle a generous amount of honey on top.
Add a lighter drizzle of chocolate syrup, less than the honey.
Sprinkle cinnamon on top.
Enjoy!

seasoning.base: a sprinkle of cinnamon
tryThis: a pinch of salt on the peanut butter

title: Dove Slush

ingredients.item: Welch's Cran-Grape juice, or Welch's grape juice

steps: Fill the blender with ice.
Add one frozen container of grape juice concentrate (Welch's is best).
Add 1 cup of Welch's Cran-Grape, or just Welch's grape juice.
Blend until smooth, but not watery.
Layer the slush in a cup with vanilla ice cream.
notes: Makes 3 to 4 cups, maybe more depending on your glass. Watch out for the brain freeze! J D prefers Welch's.

seasoning.base: none needed
